description: Patient is a retired schoolteacher living with his wife
presentation: Patient is a 77-year-old retired schoolteacher living with his wife, with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. One week ago, he awoke with sudden right-sided arm and leg weakness lasting about 30 minutes without facial droop or speech changes. He presented to a local ED the next day. CT head and MRI brain were unrevealing. His basic labs were unremarkable. Today, his ABCD2 score is 5, so I initiated dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin 81 mg indefinitely + clopidogrel 75 mg for 21 days) and ordered a 7-day Zio patch. Does the patient need further evaluation or medication adjustments?
